one_sentence: This paper argues that the Theophysical Method, which restores 'Why' to inquiry, survives scientific scrutiny and outperforms naturalism in explanatory power across foundational phenomena.
executive_summary: This document presents a comprehensive case for the Theophysical Method as a testable, falsifiable framework for cross-domain synthesis that restores the question 'Why' to scientific inquiry. It argues that the 1927 ban on 'Why' has led to fragmentation, evidenced by the replication crisis (11-62% replication rates) and disciplinary silos. The paper provides bidirectional evidence: 12 Bible-to-science claims with a 2,700-year average priority gap, and 10 empirical results naturalism cannot close. It introduces new metrics (UTDGS, 12 Structural Coherence Invariants) and compares frameworks head-to-head, finding Theophysics scores 9/10 in defense depth and integration, comparable to General Relativity. The conclusion is that both systems are circular, but theism scores 39/50 vs naturalism's 21/50 on foundational phenomena, with the framework surviving adversarial review and a live falsification test scheduled for October 2026.
short_summary: This document is a defense of the Theophysical Method as a rigorous, testable framework for cross-domain synthesis that restores 'Why' to inquiry. Its core structural claim is that the 1927 ban on 'Why' has caused fragmentation and the replication crisis, and that restoring it enables unification across 45 domains. Key evidence includes 12 Bible-to-science claims with a 2,700-year average priority gap, 10 empirical gaps naturalism cannot close, and a comparative scorecard where theism scores 39/50 vs naturalism's 21/50. This matters because it offers a falsifiable, integrated approach that addresses foundational questions in physics, theology, and information theory, with a live test scheduled for October 2026.
